narrative.overview:
QTR33 Pitwall should read like the screen a race engineer watches on the pit wall: dark, as dense as the job needs and no denser, with every pixel there so the state of the race reads in one glance. The fan has the broadcast in front of them and looks across for a second at a time. The interface has to answer in that second, then let them look back.

The system is precise and restrained. Surfaces are flat, sections are separated by whitespace and 1px hairlines, and components carry no fills, shadows or chrome of their own. Color is held back for two jobs: one interface accent, Start Light Red, and the timing-data colors that follow official convention (purple for overall fastest, green for personal best, yellow for timed, plus tyre compounds and track flags). With that much restraint, any color on screen means something.

Numbers are the hero. Every timing value is set in a tabular monospace so columns stay aligned while values change several times a second, and each screen has exactly one loud number: on the main view, laps (current/total) in a race and time remaining on the official clock in practice and qualifying; in the driver drawer, the car's position. Dark is the default theme; the light theme is a full counterpart built from the same tokens, not an inverted afterthought.
keyCharacteristics: Flat, hairline-separated layout; no shadows, gradients, blur or glow.
One interface accent (Start Light Red); all other color is timing data.
Tabular monospace numerals throughout; one hero numeral per screen.
Two weights only (400 and 600), a five-step type scale.
Ambient motion limited to the LIVE dot and the caution rule.
Dark default with an equal light theme, both WCAG AA for text.

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Start Light Red is the only interface accent. If an element needs emphasis and is not data, it gets weight or `ink`, not a new color.

rules.name: The Data Earns Color Rule
rules.body: Data colors are text color or thin bars, never box fills or backgrounds. A cell is purple because the time is the fastest, never for decoration.

rules.name: The Two Themes Rule
rules.body: Every new token is defined in both theme blocks and mapped in `tailwind.config.js`; text pairs stay at or above WCAG AA (4.5:1) on both `paper` and `raise` (rows are read while hovered or selected), and thin bars that carry meaning stay at or above 3:1 on `paper`, in both themes.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: Every timing numeral uses `.num` (IBM Plex Mono, `tnum`). A number that can change while visible is never set in proportional figures.

rules.name: The Two Weights Rule
rules.body: Only 400 and 600. Hierarchy comes from size, case and color (`ink` vs `mute`), not from extra weights.

rules.name: The One Hero Rule
rules.body: Each screen (the main view, or an open drawer) has exactly one `text-hero` number, and it is the answer the screen exists to give. A second hero on the same screen means one of them is wrong.

rules.name: The Still Columns Rule
rules.body: Values change several times a second, so no value may move its neighbours. Every timing column has a fixed width in the `colgroup`, sized to the longest real value it can hold (IBM Plex Mono 13px ≈ 7.8px per digit, plus 24px padding); Driver is the only flexible column and truncates. Rows are one line and never change height either: the position delta sits beside the number. Below `sm` (640px) the driver cell drops to number and three-letter code.

rules.name: The Glance Density Rule
rules.body: Density serves a one-second glance: whitespace and hairlines separate groups, never boxes. If a new element needs a container to be legible, the grouping is wrong.

rules.name: The Flat Monitor Rule
rules.body: No shadows, gradients, blur or glow, at rest or in any state. If a layer must read as above another, use the scrim and a hairline border.

rules.name: The Only Movers Rule
rules.body: Two things may animate continuously: the LIVE dot and the caution alert rule. Everything else is static, apart from 150ms color transitions on hover and the dialog's entry. All of it collapses under `prefers-reduced-motion`.

dos: Do use the token names (`paper`, `raise`, `ink`, `mute`, `rule`, `signal`, data tokens) through Tailwind classes; add new tokens to both theme blocks in `index.css` and to `tailwind.config.js`.
Do set every timing numeral in `.num` (IBM Plex Mono, tabular).
Do give each screen exactly one `text-hero` number: laps or time remaining on the main view, the position in the driver drawer.
Do say "Leader" once on P1 (in Gap) and leave its Interval empty.
Do present single values in the drawer as Stats (Label over Numeral Large) and put units in the section heading.
Do separate groups with whitespace and 1px `rule` hairlines.
Do color times by meaning only: `best` for overall fastest, `pb` for personal best, `ink` otherwise.
Do keep the global 2px `signal` focus outline visible on every interactive element.
Do check both themes for WCAG AA text contrast before shipping.
donts: Don't fill unknown facts with defaults: a missing team, total or session name stays empty or reads "—".
Don't hard-code colors or use `dark:` variants. A team with no color from the feed gets a `rule` bar, never an invented brand color; browser surfaces (text selection, scrollbars) take tokens too.
Don't add shadows, gradients, blur or glow.
Don't use data colors as box fills or backgrounds.
Don't introduce a second interface accent.
Don't use weights other than 400 and 600.
Don't animate anything besides the LIVE dot and the caution alert rule.
Don't use official Formula 1 logos or marks; the product is unofficial.
